## 1. Time and Tsibbles

This analysis uses two monthly time-series datasets: U.S. retail and food services sales and Canadian natural gas production. The retail dataset contains seasonally adjusted (RSAFS) and non-seasonally adjusted (RSAFSNA) sales data beginning in 1992. The Canadian natural gas dataset contains monthly production volumes from January 1960 through February 2005.

The retail data is organized as a tsibble with Month as the index and series_id as the key, allowing both retail series to be analyzed separately. The Canadian natural gas data uses Month as its index and does not require a key because it contains only one series.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(fpp3)

retail_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/retail_sales_raw.csv",
  na = ".",
  col_types = cols(
    observation_date = col_date(format = "%Y-%m-%d"),
    RSAFS = col_double(),
    RSAFSNA = col_double()
  )
)

retail_raw_long <- retail_raw |>
  select(observation_date, RSAFS, RSAFSNA) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(RSAFS, RSAFSNA),
    names_to = "series_id",
    values_to = "sales"
  )

retail_ts <- retail_raw_long |>
  mutate(Month = yearmonth(observation_date)) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Month, key = series_id)

can_gas <- canadian_gas |>
  select(Month, Volume)
```

```{r}
retail_ts |>
  head() |>
  as_tibble() |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "First Six Observations of U.S. Retail Sales"
  )

# Canadian natural gas data
can_gas |>
  head() |>
  as_tibble() |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "First Six Observations of Canadian Natural Gas Production"
  )
```


```{r}
retail_ts |>
  autoplot(sales) +
  labs(
    title = "U.S. Retail and Food Services Sales",
    subtitle = "Seasonally adjusted vs. not seasonally adjusted",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Millions of dollars",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r}
can_gas |>
  autoplot(Volume) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Canadian Natural Gas Production with Trend",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Billions of cubic metres"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The non-seasonally adjusted retail sales series shows noticeable repeating spikes and drops throughout each year, while the seasonally adjusted series is much smoother. Both series follow a similar long-run upward trend and experience larger economic fluctuations around the same periods.

Canadian natural gas production also shows a long-run upward trend with repeating seasonal fluctuations. Adding a smoothed trend line makes it easier to identify the overall increase in production despite the monthly variation.
